ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, it is known that $\angle MON=30^\circ$, points $A_1$, $A_2$, $A_3$, ... are on ray $ON$, and points $B_1$, $B_2$, $B_3$, ... are on ray $OM$. The triangles $\triangle A_1B_1A_2$, $\triangle A_2B_2A_3$, $\triangle A_3B_3A_4$, ... are all equilateral triangles. If $OA_1=3$, what is the side length of $\triangle A_{10}B_{10}A_{11}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle MON=30^\circ$ and $\angle B_{1}A_{1}A_{2}=60^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle OB_{1}A_{1}=\angle B_{1}A_{1}A_{2}-\angle MON=30^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle MON=\angle OB_{1}A_{1}$.\\
Thus, we have $A_{1}O=B_{1}A_{1}=3$.\\
Consequently, $A_{2}O=A_{1}O+A_{1}A_{2}=3\times 2$.\\
Similarly, we can deduce $AO_{3}=A_{3}B_{3}=3\times 2^{2}$.\\
Following the same pattern $A_{4}O=A_{4}B_{4}=3\times 2^{3}$.\\
$A_{5}O=A_{5}B_{5}=3\times 2^{4}$.\\
$\cdots$\\
$A_{n}O=A_{n}B_{n}=3\times 2^{n-1}$.\\
Therefore, the side length of $\triangle A_{10}B_{10}A_{11}$ is $3\times 2^{9}=\boxed{1536}$.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/trigonometric route. First read the diagram: take ON as the x-axis with O at the origin, and take OM as the ray making 30° above it; A_n is on the x-axis and B_n is on the slanted ray. From the text, set OA1 = 3, so A1 has coordinate x1 = 3, and each triangle A_nB_nA_{n+1} is equilateral. Let A_n = (x_n, 0), let the side length be s_n, so A_{n+1} = (x_n + s_n, 0). Because the equilateral triangle is built above the base, its apex is B_n = (x_n + s_n/2, (sqrt(3)/2)s_n). raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, it is known that $\angle MON=30^\circ$, points $A_1$, $A_2$, $A_3$, ... are on ray $ON$, and points $B_1$, $B_2$, $B_3$, ... are on ray $OM$. The triangles $\triangle A_1B_1A_2$, $\triangle A_2B_2A_3$, $\triangle A_3B_3A_4$, ... are all equilateral triangles. If $OA_1=3$, what is the side length of $\triangle A_{10}B_{10}A_{11}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle MON=30^\circ$ and $\angle B_{1}A_{1}A_{2}=60^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle OB_{1}A_{1}=\angle B_{1}A_{1}A_{2}-\angle MON=30^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle MON=\angle OB_{1}A_{1}$.\\
Thus, we have $A_{1}O=B_{1}A_{1}=3$.\\
Consequently, $A_{2}O=A_{1}O+A_{1}A_{2}=3\times 2$.\\
Similarly, we can deduce $AO_{3}=A_{3}B_{3}=3\times 2^{2}$.\\
Following the same pattern $A_{4}O=A_{4}B_{4}=3\times 2^{3}$.\\
$A_{5}O=A_{5}B_{5}=3\times 2^{4}$.\\
$\cdots$\\
$A_{n}O=A_{n}B_{n}=3\times 2^{n-1}$.\\
Therefore, the side length of $\triangle A_{10}B_{10}A_{11}$ is $3\times 2^{9}=\boxed{1536}$

Reasoning: Let the side length of the nth equilateral triangle A_nB_nA_{n+1} be s_n. Because A_n and A_{n+1} are both on ON, A_nA_{n+1} is along ray ON; also because triangle A_nB_nA_{n+1} is an equilateral triangle, the angle between side A_nB_n and ON is 60°. The angle between ray OM and ON is 30°, and B_n is on OM, so in triangle OA_nB_n, ∠A_nOB_n = 30°, and ∠OB_nA_n = 60° - 30° = 30°. Therefore triangle OA_nB_n has two equal angles, giving OA_n = A_nB_n. That is to say, s_n = A_nB_n = OA_n.
Also because OA_{n+1} = OA_n + A_nA_{n+1}, while A_nA_{n+1} = s_n = OA_n, so OA_{n+1} = 2OA_n. It is known that OA_1 = 3, therefore OA_n = 3·2^{n-1}. The side length of the 10th equilateral triangle A_{10}B_{10}A_{11} is s_{10} = OA_{10} = 3·2^9 = 1536.
